Obeliai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžys County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Obeliai's Jewish community, dating to the 16th century, was divided between Hasidic and Misnagdim factions who prayed separately and, per the source, harbored 'great hostilities' toward one another. On August 25, 1941, armed Lithuanians took the town's Jews, together with refugees from nearby villages, to Antanoshe village and murdered them; a German source itemized the toll at 112 men, 627 women, and 421 children. Obeliai's most remarkable native son was Joe Slovo (born Yossel Mashel Slovo), who emigrated to South Africa and became a leading anti-apartheid figure — a theorist and long-time leader of the South African Communist Party, a senior figure in the African National Congress, and a government minister under Nelson Mandela. Descendants of the town, led by Rabbi Mayer Abramowitz, renovated and rededicated this cemetery in 2003.
